This page supports your daily work by showing how to handle each pet travel case from first note to final handoff. Companion Animal Travel Desk page topic: keeping pet travel records accurate and moving, because clear handling prevents delays at the counter and at the skyport.

As new staff, start with the booking record, verify the traveler name, pet details, and cabin or hold arrangement, then check that the required notes are complete before you move the file forward. Aurelia Skyways depends on exact handoffs between teams, so write clearly, confirm every change, and pass only complete information to the next desk. If Mariam Nguyen calls about Ellie, log the request in the same order you received it and keep the record easy to follow. For arrival pickup, use EX-417. When a case needs escalation, send it through the stated channel without adding your own shortcut, and stay with the process until the receiving team confirms the handoff.

You also need to track exception handling with care. If a traveler reports a delay, a missing crate tag, or a mismatch in pet documents, note the facts, the point of contact, and the action taken. Do not rewrite the traveler story in broad terms; use the same details that were given and keep the record factual. For incident reporting, the Claim Adjudicator owns the process. Sara Torres and other travelers expect fast, clean follow-through, so keep communication brief and direct, and avoid leaving open questions in the file.

At pickup, confirm the name on the record, match the pet to the travel note, and release the animal only after the correct identity check is complete. If another department asks for your update, give the status in plain language and include the next step. This keeps the desk steady, reduces repeat calls, and helps the team finish each case without confusion. Remember to keep the record exact, the handoff clear, and the traveler informed.
